command:
set +e
set -uo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp
cd /tmp
: > ssrc.log; : > search_bsa.log; : > fdr.log

# spawn runs task commands under bash -e; `set -uo pipefail` does not clear it (spawn#707).
# PATH export IS needed: aarchbio images have their PATH dropped by the task shell.
# The identity checks live in the staged identities.py, not inline: a task command rides in
# EC2 user data, capped at 16,384 bytes, and the inline version would not launch.

echo "== staged bytes must match their pins =="
# pins.sha256 covers every input the RECIPE stages; this task stages a subset of them, so
# --ignore-missing is required -- plain `sha256sum -c` fails on a file it was never given.
# That flag alone would pass vacuously if nothing were staged, so the number actually verified
# is asserted too.
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing pins.sha256 || { echo "FAIL: a staged file does not match its pin"; exit 1; }
NOK=$(sha256sum -c --ignore-missing pins.sha256 2>/dev/null | grep -c ': OK$')
printf 'pinned_files_verified\t%s\n' "$NOK"
test "$NOK" -eq 9 || { echo "FAIL: verified $NOK pinned files, expected 9"; exit 1; }
sed 's/^/  /' expected.tsv
DBT=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="db_targets"{print $2}' expected.tsv)
DBD=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="db_decoys"{print $2}'  expected.tsv)

echo "== every tool this chain needs must be present =="
# Check all of them before running any, so a missing tool is a clear message rather than a
# failure three steps in. CometAdapter and MSGFPlusAdapter exist in this image but are only
# WRAPPERS -- the Comet and MSGF+ binaries are not shipped -- which is why the search engine
# here is OpenMS's own SimpleSearchEngine.
for t in SimpleSearchEngine PeptideIndexer FalseDiscoveryRate; do
  if command -v "$t" >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '  tool %-22s present\n' "$t"
  else printf '  tool %-22s MISSING\n' "$t"; MISSING=1; fi
done
test -z "${MISSING:-}" || { echo "FAIL: a required TOPP tool is absent from this image"; exit 1; }

# =========================================================== LEG A: the committed reproduction
# SimpleSearchEngine ships its own test spectra, database, .ini and expected idXML. Passing the
# committed .ini is what makes this a reproduction rather than a similar run -- it sets
# threads=1, fragment tolerance 0.1 Da, empty fixed mods and variable Oxidation (M). Explicit
# -in/-database/-out override the .ini's absolute paths from the committer's machine.
echo "== LEG A: reproduce SimpleSearchEngine's own committed output =="
SimpleSearchEngine -ini SimpleSearchEngine_1.ini \
  -in SimpleSearchEngine_1.mzML -database SimpleSearchEngine_1.fasta \
  -out ref_out.idXML > ssrc.log 2>&1
RC=$?
if [ "$RC" != "0" ]; then
  grep -iE "Unknown option|Invalid|error message" ssrc.log | grep -v "valid:" | head -5
  echo "FAIL: SimpleSearchEngine exited $RC on its own test fixture"; exit 1
fi
test -s ref_out.idXML || { echo "FAIL: leg A produced no output"; exit 1; }

# =============================================== LEG B: the real run, with a target-decoy FDR
# Parameters follow the committed OMSSA reference where the tool permits: same database, same
# enzyme, same missed cleavages, same +1..+3 charges, same 0.05 Da precursor window. Fragment
# tolerance CANNOT match -- the reference used 0.3 Da and SimpleSearchEngine's deisotoper
# refuses anything above 0.1 Da -- so this run searches 3x tighter, which costs sensitivity on
# low-resolution MS2 and is why the peptide overlap is asserted as a floor, not an equality.
echo "== LEG B: search 1,120 MS2 spectra against $DBT+$DBD target/decoy =="
T0=$(date +%s)
SimpleSearchEngine -in BSA1.mzML -database db.fasta -out psm.idXML \
  -Search:enzyme Trypsin \
  -Search:precursor:mass_tolerance 0.05 -Search:precursor:mass_tolerance_unit Da \
  -Search:fragment:mass_tolerance 0.1   -Search:fragment:mass_tolerance_unit Da \
  -Search:precursor:min_charge 1 -Search:precursor:max_charge 3 \
  -Search:peptide:missed_cleavages 1 \
  -Search:modifications:variable "Oxidation (M)" \
  -threads 1 > search_bsa.log 2>&1
RC=$?
T1=$(date +%s)
printf 'bsa_search_rc\t%s\nbsa_search_wall_s\t%s\n' "$RC" "$((T1-T0))"
if [ "$RC" != "0" ]; then
  grep -iE "Unknown option|Invalid|error message" search_bsa.log | grep -v "valid:" | head -5
  echo "FAIL: the BSA search exited $RC"; exit 1
fi
test -s psm.idXML || { echo "FAIL: no PSMs written"; exit 1; }

echo "== assign target/decoy status by the _rev SUFFIX, then estimate FDR =="
# The database marks decoys with a _rev suffix. Passing a prefix convention here would label
# every decoy a target and the FDR estimate would be silently meaningless.
PeptideIndexer -in psm.idXML -fasta db.fasta -out indexed.idXML \
  -decoy_string _rev -decoy_string_position suffix -missing_decoy_action warn \
  >> fdr.log 2>&1
test "$?" = "0" || { tail -25 fdr.log; echo "FAIL: PeptideIndexer failed"; exit 1; }
# -protein defaults to TRUE, and protein-level FDR needs an inference step this recipe does
# not do, so the tool refuses outright ("protein inference was not yet performed"). It is
# right to: every identity here is PSM-level, so ask for PSM-level and nothing else rather
# than reaching for -force and accepting a number that would not mean anything.
# add_decoy_peptides keeps the decoy PSMs in the output -- by default the tool uses them to
# estimate FDR and then DISCARDS them (957 -> 513 here), which breaks the row join and throws
# away the only evidence the FDR estimate rests on. Their q-value is BORROWED from the nearest
# target, so the checks count decoys by SCORE, never by q.
#
# It lives in the `algorithm` subsection, which this tool does NOT accept as
# `-algorithm:add_decoy_peptides` on the command line -- it answers by printing its usage. The
# documented route is -write_ini, so the default INI is generated, the one value flipped, and
# the flip ASSERTED: a silently failed sed would leave decoys out of the output.
FalseDiscoveryRate -write_ini fdr.ini > /dev/null 2>&1
test -s fdr.ini || { echo "FAIL: could not write the default FalseDiscoveryRate INI"; exit 1; }
sed -i 's|\(name="add_decoy_peptides" *value="\)false|\1true|' fdr.ini
grep -q 'name="add_decoy_peptides" *value="true"' fdr.ini \
  || { grep -o 'name="add_decoy_peptides"[^/]*' fdr.ini
       echo "FAIL: add_decoy_peptides is still false in the INI"; exit 1; }
echo "  add_decoy_peptides set to true in the generated INI"
FalseDiscoveryRate -ini fdr.ini -in indexed.idXML -out fdr.idXML \
  -PSM true -protein false >> fdr.log 2>&1
test "$?" = "0" || { tail -25 fdr.log; echo "FAIL: FalseDiscoveryRate failed"; exit 1; }
# The checks read indexed.idXML and fdr.idXML directly. They are in shell, not Python: this
# image ships no interpreter -- a single-tool bioconda image around a C++ toolkit, so python3
# is absent even with /opt/conda/bin on PATH.
bash identities.sh 2>&1 | tee identities.log
test "${PIPESTATUS[0]}" = "0" || { echo "FAIL: an identity failed"; exit 1; }

cp score.tsv proteomics-diag.txt
uname -m | awk '{print "arch\t"$1}'
echo "DONE"
